summary.headline: Globus Spirits Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 2% YoY to INR63.8 crores; manufacturing EBITDA fell to INR4.6/litre, with INR5-7/litre guidance maintained.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR758 crores (up 15% YoY) and EBITDA INR63.8 crores (up 2% YoY), while H1 EBITDA rose 17% to INR143.3 crores. Manufacturing EBITDA per litre dropped to INR4.6 on seasonal grain and fuel inflation and plant maintenance, with H1 at INR5.59 and trailing 12 months at about INR6.6. Management kept the INR5-7 per litre annual manufacturing guidance, citing the 2026-27 ethanol year and lower broken-rice and maize prices. The INR200 crore QIP was completed, with about INR155 crores used to repay debt and debt-to-EBITDA falling from 2.63x to about 2x.

financial_highlights.value: INR4.6/litre (EBITDA INR25.4 crores on 55.26 million litres)
financial_highlights.change: H1 INR5.59/litre; trailing 12 months about INR6.6/litre

segments.name: Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR455 crores on 55.26 million litres with EBITDA INR25.4 crores (INR4.6/litre), hit by grain and fuel costs and plant maintenance. Management guides INR5-7/litre annually and expects higher utilisation in the 2026-27 ethanol year.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR59.9 crores (+54% YoY, +9% QoQ) on 0.46 million cases (+64% YoY); EBITDA loss narrowed to INR0.2 crores. H1 revenue about INR114.9 crores on about 0.88 million cases; 5 of 12 footprint states are profitable.

segments.name: Regular & Others (R&O)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR242.8 crores (+14% YoY) on 4.24 million cases (+16% YoY); EBITDA INR38.6 crores (+4% YoY), a margin moderation vs Q1 on lower sequential volume. H1 revenue about INR499.2 crores and EBITDA INR82.6 crores; growth is mainly from UP.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guidance of INR5-7 per litre maintained on an annual basis; H1 was below range, and management hopes for higher H2 realisations as maize and rice prices cool after Diwali.
R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 16-18% reiterated; a separate comment cited a range of 15-18%.
Interest savings of about INR6 crores in H2 FY27 (INR11-12 crores annualised) from debt repayment and refinancing.
P&A next phase: 5 additional duty-free channels and entry into 2 new states in FY27; CSG entry targeted in Q3 subject to approvals.
Management expects higher capacity utilisation in the 2026-27 ethanol year (from November) as sugar-based ethanol supply falls; it does not expect to raise the per-litre margin guidance.
Management plans to re-enter West Bengal in FY28 and is re-evaluating Delhi plans given weak industry volumes; West Bengal sales are currently zero.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity of about 20-25 crore litres annually; utilisation has been 80-85%, expected to rise meaningfully in the coming year.
UP distilleries are not yet at full utilisation; UP utilisation has risen in the last 3-4 months as UP shifts from molasses-based to grain-based country liquor.
Rajasthan has headroom of about 400,000-500,000 cases a month, subject to a state ceiling; no plans to expand Rajasthan capacity, with capital focused on consumer business.
Behror unit is largely for internal consumption and was excluded from the discussion.
QIP of INR200 crores completed; about INR150-155 crores used for debt repayment and the balance held as liquid funds, which may fund bottling and whisky-related expansion.
demand_pricing: Management expects about 900 crore litres of grain-based ethanol demand from OMCs, with chemical use of 100-150 crore litres and beverage use of 300-400 crore litres.
Maize-based ethanol was about 60% of H1 ethanol sales; management says it could fall to about 30% as the product mix shifts with profitability.
September-end grain prices were about INR27-28/kg for rice and INR23-24/kg for maize, versus INR24-25 and INR21-22 at end-Q1; these are end-period, not average, prices.
Management expects broken rice supply to rise as FCI moves to 10% broken content from 25%, which should keep rice prices subdued.
Power and fuel cost was INR6.3/kg in Q2, up 10-11% QoQ, totalling about INR60.43 crores for the quarter.
Rajasthan R&O grows low-to-mid single-digit volume plus 4-6% annual price increases; Globus holds about 50% of the private 60% of the market.
Management said packaging material inflation linked to oil prices was an unusual headwind this year.
ENA export volume was about 5 million litres in H1; exports are not tracked as a separate business.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR5-7/litre manufacturing guidance hold after the INR3/litre cut in maize-based ethanol prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said maize prices should stay lower, citing FCI rice allocation clarity and more broken rice; the ENA and ethanol flexibility keeps the guidance intact. It acknowledged Q2 at 4.6-4.7/litre.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R&O EBITDA fall in Q2, and how much did UP contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to commodity cycle timing, with Q2 the peak of raw material and fuel inflation. Rajasthan grows mid-single digits in volume; almost all incremental R&O growth came from UP.

qa_highlights.question: Will UP margins converge with Rajasthan, and is the R&O margin range changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-18% R&O EBITDA margin range; Rajasthan sits at the higher end and UP at the lower end, with UP improving as scale builds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR200 crore QIP proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crores repaid debt and the balance is liquid, to fund IMFL growth, bottling and whisky expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How will the end of sugar-based ethanol affect volumes and ENA prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects much higher volumes in the Nov-Oct ethanol year and sees a large capacity base in India, so it will not raise per-litre margin guidance. Long-term offtake covers all units except Bihar.

qa_highlights.question: Will P&A reach breakeven, and what is the growth-versus-profit trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would prioritise growth over profit while the balance sheet and cash flows allow, with profitability to follow as spending is pulled back.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Delhi, West Bengal and Haryana?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi allocation rose but industry sales are weak, so plans are being re-evaluated. West Bengal is zero now with re-entry planned in FY28; Haryana contributes but is growing slowly.

risks_watch: Manufacturing margin pressure in H1 (INR4.6/litre in Q2) from grain, fuel and packaging inflation; H2 recovery depends on maize and rice prices cooling after Diwali.
Maize-based ethanol profitability after the INR3/litre price cut; the product mix may shift toward FCI rice and broken rice.
Possible industry-wide shift into ENA that could pressure ENA prices, though management believes state-level logistics limit this.
P&A remains loss-making (EBITDA loss INR0.2 crores); growth is being prioritised over profit.
Operating cash flow fell to INR139 crores from INR270 crores as receivables rose; monitor working capital.
Delhi market compression and West Bengal absence; watch whether UP growth can offset them.
Rajasthan capacity ceiling, with about 400,000-500,000 cases a month of headroom.
Sustainability of the 16-18% R&O margin as UP mix rises, and the 15-18% range management cited elsewhere.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term manufacturing guidance and the balance sheet, though the Q2 margin dip was explained away as seasonal. Management was evasive on specifics such as state-wise UP sizing, ENA realisations and outlet-level shelf data, and deferred several questions to follow-up calls.
key_quotes: The manufacturing business is sort of steady at that range, 5% to 7% with a 20 crores to 25 crores litre kind of capacity, kind of sale annually.
So it's a conscious decision to chase growth given the strength of the balance sheet and the strength of our cash flows.
I would not look at the revenue of the company as a sort of homogeneous number.

growth.why: Management kept INR5-7/litre manufacturing EBITDA and 16-18% R&O margin guidance and expects utilisation (currently 80-85%) to be meaningfully higher in FY27 as UP grain-based volumes and ethanol-year demand rise, but gave no specific new capacity, orders or contracts behind it, and H1 manufacturing margin is below range.
